thread_a.role: rtnetlink FIB create path increments counter

thread_b.role: netdevsim FIB free work decrements counter

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([rmw(fib_info_cnt++)]) from thread_a (the counter update must not interleave with a conflicting concurrent update)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: in the vuln version neither path holds a shared lock for the counter: fib_create_info increments fib_info_cnt outside fib_info_lock and free_fib_info decrements it with no lock at all (it once relied on RTNL, no longer held by the netdevsim workqueue) -> no serialize(g) makes the two RMWs mutually exclusive
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(region [read,write]) of a counter read-modify-write broken by a concurrent interleaving update of the same scalar -> lost-update atomicity violation (KCSAN reports it generically as a data race, but rho's shape is an RMW region, not a single access)

fix_maps_to: patch moves both updates under fib_info_lock (increment at hlist insert, decrement in fib_release_info) and uses READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE for the sizing read -> adds serialize(fib_info_lock, counter update) that establishes the atomic requirement
recall_risk_notes: Strongest of the KCSAN-annotation cases: the fix is a real lock (serialize via fib_info_lock), so the missing guarantee is a concrete missing lock, exactly what the design targets, and the counter is in the static surface with both contexts (rtnetlink notifier vs netdevsim workqueue) findable. Risks: the object is a bare global scalar (surface records it as generic 'resource'), and the design must infer the implicit atomic(update) intent for a counter rather than treating it as a benign statistic; cross-context MHP (notifier chain vs workqueue) must connect.
